composing_units: 5th Armored Division; 83rd Infantry Division; 90th Infantry Division

current_activity: receiving its first Third Army mission, to protect the Avranches corridor
notes: Event date: Breakout-22 p424: early on 1 August Haislip learned that the projected southwestern operation was cancelled and a new one would go southeast; his first combat mission was to enter the gap between the diverging VIII and VII Corps (Avranches to Brécey) as a protective barrier, with the 5th Armored, 83rd and 90th Divisions (assignment still changing). Event definition: first mission order; XV Corps was to become operational upon commitment of Third Army (p423). Location: sector point at the corridor, not the corps command post (CMH list: Périers 30 July, Marcilly 4 August). Relationship: Third Army assigned.
Wikipedia: XV Corps (Haislip) took Le Mans on 8 August; Breakout-22 covers the Third Army drive east from Brittany.

current_activity: halting at Argentan on Bradley's order
notes: Breakout-25 p504: early on the afternoon of 13 August the XV Corps attack stopped; Patton told Haislip not to go beyond Argentan and to recall elements near Falaise.

current_activity: 79th Division crossing the Seine at Mantes-Gassicourt
notes: Breakout-28 p577: the 79th Division started across the Seine on the evening of 19 August near Mantes.

current_activity: crossing the Seine at Mantes-Gassicourt with the 79th Division
notes: Event date: CMH "Northern France": Haislip's XV Corps drove sixty miles to Dreux and established a Seine bridgehead at Mantes-Gassicourt on the night of 19-20 August (the 79th Division crossed on the morning of 20 August). Event definition: river crossing and bridgehead. Location: the CMH command-post list gives the corps at Mantes-la-Jolie on 20 August; commune centroid, not the bridgehead line. Relationship: Third Army assigned until 24 August.

current_activity: passing from Third Army to First Army control at 0600
notes: Event date: Breakout-28 p578: at 0600 on 24 August XV Corps passed from the control of Third Army to that of First Army; Hodges told Haislip to clear the zone for British Second Army elements and to move the 5th Armored south. Event definition: control of the corps moves from Third Army to First Army; the row records First Army operational control. Relationship: First Army operational control from 0600 on 24 August is documented and ends on 29 August (C0503). Third Army assigned is inferred continuity (see the relationship note): Lorraine ch. IV says the corps was taken from Third Army and later returned, the Third Army After Action Report says it was released to First Army, and Wikipedia's subordination table shows First Army only for 24-28 August (secondary), so no source documents a retained Third Army assignment. Location: the CMH command-post list (World War II by Day) has the corps at Mantes-la-Jolie on 20 and on 28 August and no entry between. The Mantes vicinity is inferred from those two entries; it is not claimed that the headquarters stayed there without moving, and on 24 August it may have been elsewhere in the area. The row uses the 20 August entry (four days earlier; 28 August is four days later). Event support: high (Green Book, dated to the hour). Location support: low (command post listed four days earlier).

current_activity: handing the Mantes bridgehead to XIX Corps and moving for Third Army
notes: Event date: Breakout-31 p672: at noon on 29 August XIX Corps took command of the three divisions in the Mantes bridgehead as the XV Corps headquarters started for an assembly area southeast of Paris and eventual Third Army assignment; the CMH list shows Saint-Léger-en-Yvelines on 29 August and Rozay-en-Brie on 30 August. Event definition: XV Corps gives up the Mantes bridgehead; First Army operational control ends and Third Army control resumes. Relationship: First Army operational control carries an explicit end on 29 August (the hour is not documented, only that the headquarters left at noon); Third Army operational control is restored from 29 August (Third Army After Action Report; Lorraine ch. IV) and the standing assignment during these days is inferred, as in C0502. Third Army 'assigned' is not re-listed because no source uses that word for 29 August. Location: Saint-Léger commune centroid, a stop on the move. Event support: high (Green Book, noon 29 August; Third Army After Action Report). Location support: moderate (CMH list, same day).
Wikipedia: XV Corps crossed the Moselle at Charmes on 12 September; Lorraine Campaign chapter 2 covers the Moselle crossings.

current_activity: attacks from Lunéville toward Sarrebourg and the Saverne Gap
notes: Event date: 13 November 1944 (Riviera ch22: Patch set the date of the XV Corps attack for 13 November; ch24: Haislip's XV Corps led off on 13 November in the north). Event definition: Seventh Army's northern corps opens the 6th Army Group November offensive toward the Saverne Gap; VI Corps follows within two days of plan and Bethouart's II Corps (French) one day later. The Green Book citations are chapter level (the HyperWar page lacks a page marker for these passages). Relationship: Seventh Army assigned from 29 September (Riviera p253: control of the corps officially passed to the 6th Army Group and the Seventh Army on that day; the Third Army link on C0332 ends the same day); 6th Army Group above it. Location: The atlas lists the corps command post at Lunéville from 8 October (also seen in the Green Book photo caption of October); the next entry is Sarrebourg, 23 November. Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Lunéville. Event support: high (two Green Book statements). Location support: low (36 days to the nearest earlier atlas entry).
